summary: the level blockout: Game-boy's attack arcs in the director, the level kit, then the graybox Mission 1 level from the reference, start to boss
read_first: docs/milestones/M5-plan.md §1 (only the decisions your brief names) and §2 'Tuning' and 'File ownership'
note: Phase 2. Game-boy approved reference/encounters.md as drafted, with no changes (2026-11-03, "OK, enemy arcs are good. Let's continue with the rest of M5 now"): build exactly its arenas, waves, spawn sides and pickups. The rear-warning question took its default: Punks never come round behind on their own, which the merged arcs already do, so no director change is wanted. ARC, KIT and BOT are merged into m5/level-blockout. STREET, ROOF and FINALE build at the same time and own disjoint files (plan §2 'File ownership' and 'Level space'): build only inside your own footprint. The lead merges STREET, ROOF, then FINALE, and runs the whole level after.

read: docs/milestones/M5-plan.md §1 D7-D11, §2 'Level kit', 'Scene conventions', 'Level space', 'File ownership'
packages.note: From KIT (M5-calls/KIT.md): copy the strip's node patterns. Each arena has LockTrigger, Respawn and SpawnPoints with a LanePoint; the seam shutter is the ExitBarrier. A HazardVolume must cover the whole void past an edge, with its catch floor at a depth no floor height is within 0.3 m of. A car barrier needs room beside the opening to slide aside (a side street or an alley mouth of its width), or it pops through geometry. A stair flight belongs to the arena below, so the lower arena's lock volume runs up to the barrier. Stairs are LevelStairs (walking bodies ride a hidden glide ramp on layer 9). Record with BOT's level_bot (BOT_SCENE=res://tests/bot/level_bot.tscn, CAPTURE_ARGS="--level=<your section scene>"), and judge the plain first-person view.
